papers.title: LncPNdeep: A long non-coding RNA classifier based on large language model with peptide and nucleotide embedding.
papers.abstract: Accurate classification of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) is essential for transcriptome annotation and understanding gene regulation. Existing computational methods predominantly rely on nucleotide sequence features, frequently overlooking biologically relevant peptide signals encoded within lncRNAs. To overcome this limitation, we developed LncPNdeep, an integrative deep learning framework that combines nucleotide and peptide embeddings extracted via masked language models, specifically utilizing contextual representations from BigBird, Longformer, and ProtTrans. By fusing both features in a
papers.summary: LncPNdeep is a new deep learning tool that classifies long non-coding RNAs by combining both nucleotide and peptide sequence information using large language models, which improves accuracy over methods that only use nucleotide features. This approach captures biologically relevant peptide signals within lncRNAs that were previously overlooked.

papers.title: ISUP Grade Group Migration Between Prostate Biopsy and Radical Prostatectomy: A Systematic Review of Emerging Predictors.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) Grade Group discordance between prostate biopsy and radical prostatectomy (RP) affects 25-50% of men with localized prostate cancer and has direct implications for active surveillance, nerve-sparing, and adjuvant-treatment decisions. We synthesized contemporary evidence on the frequency of biopsy-to-RP grade migration and on emerging imaging, molecular/genomic, and artificial-intelligence (AI)-based predictors of migration. Methods: MEDLINE (PubMed) was searched from 1 January 2010 to 5 May 2026, supplemented by citati
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on ISUP Grade Group discordance between prostate biopsy and radical prostatectomy, which affects 25-50% of men with localized prostate cancer and impacts treatment decisions. It highlights emerging imaging, molecular/genomic, and AI-based predictors that may help identify patients at risk of grade migration.

papers.title: AI-Guided Long Non-Coding RNA Target Discovery for Precision Medicine: Integrating GWAS, Multi-Omics, Experimental Validation, and RNA Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Precision medicine requires translation of genetic and molecular variation into clinically actionable therapeutic targets. However, many disease-associated signals identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS) reside in non-coding regulatory regions, making biological interpretation and therapeutic prioritization difficult. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are regulatory molecules with growing relevance to disease mechanisms, biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and RNA-based therapeutics. This review presents a translational framework for AI-guided lncRNA t
papers.summary: This review outlines a framework for using AI to identify long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) as therapeutic targets, integrating GWAS data, multi-omics, and experimental validation. It highlights the role of lncRNAs in precision medicine and RNA-based therapeutics, addressing challenges in interpreting non-coding disease-associated variants.

papers.title: A First-Trimester Serum Proteomic Signature for Early Prediction of Preeclampsia: Integrated Untargeted and Targeted Mass Spectrometry with Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: First-trimester prediction of preeclampsia (PE) remains a major clinical challenge, particularly outside specialized fetal medicine centers. This study aimed to identify and validate serum protein biomarkers for early PE prediction using an integrated proteomic approach. A prospective cohort of 64 first-trimester singleton pregnancies (32 future PE cases, 32 matched controls) was analyzed. Untargeted proteomics was performed using DIA-PASEF-MS, followed by targeted cross-platform verification with MRM-MS. Machine learning classifiers (support vector machines, SVM, and random forest) were train
papers.summary: This study identifies a serum proteomic signature in the first trimester that can predict preeclampsia before clinical onset, using an integrated mass spectrometry approach and machine learning. The findings suggest a promising blood-based test for early PE risk assessment, potentially improving outcomes through earlier surveillance and intervention.

papers.title: iDCF: Interpretable deconvolution of cell fractions via biologically-informed deep learning using scRNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: Precise resolution of cellular heterogeneity within complex tissues is fundamental to deciphering disease etiologies from bulk transcriptomic profiles. While computational deconvolution offers a scalable alternative, current deep learning methods predominantly operate as "black boxes," neglecting the structural constraints of biological laws. This reliance on purely data-driven feature extraction often yields biologically incoherent predictions and limited mechanistic interpretability. iDCF (Interpretable Deconvolution of Cell Fractions) is a novel framework that enforces biological topology o
papers.summary: iDCF is a new deep-learning framework for deconvolving cell-type fractions from bulk RNA-seq data that explicitly incorporates biological structure (cell-type hierarchy) into the model, improving interpretability and biological coherence over black-box approaches. It leverages scRNA-seq reference data to guide training and yields more reliable cell fraction estimates.

papers.title: Model-guided design of defined microbial community reveals interactions underpinning plant growth and stress tolerance.
papers.abstract: Defined microbial communities (DMCs; also known as SynComs) offer a promising strategy to enhance plant growth and stress tolerance by harnessing beneficial plant-associated microbes. However, the rational design and efficient exploration of complex DMC configurations remain challenging. Here, we present an interpretable model-guided framework that integrates plant phenotyping, microbial genomics, and machine learning to optimize DMC outcomes and identify microbial interactions relevant to plant performance. Using tomato as a model, we evaluated diverse DMC, temperature, and metabolite combina
papers.summary: This study presents an interpretable machine-learning framework that integrates plant phenotyping, microbial genomics, and experimental data to guide the design of defined microbial communities (SynComs) for enhancing plant growth and stress tolerance in tomato. The model identifies key microbial interactions and environmental factors, offering a rational approach to optimize community composition for desired plant outcomes.

papers.title: Challenges and opportunities in type III secretion system effector prediction.
papers.abstract: Type III secretion system effectors (T3SEs) are small bacterial proteins with big biological roles. They act as central molecular mediators of interactions between Gram-negative bacteria and eukaryotic hosts, spanning pathogenic, symbiotic and environmental contexts. Over the past three decades, T3SE discovery has progressed from genome-independent experimental assays to an expanding landscape of computational prediction methods. Early in silico approaches formalized empirically defined protein N-terminal properties into feature-engineered machine-learning models, followed by deep-learning met
papers.summary: This review discusses the evolution and current state of computational methods for predicting type III secretion system effectors (T3SEs), from early feature-engineered machine learning to modern deep-learning approaches. It highlights ongoing challenges, such as limited training data and the need for better generalization across bacterial species, while pointing to opportunities for improving prediction accuracy through advanced models and integration of biological context.

papers.title: CompBio and MIRaS-a multi-omic analysis platform built on a memory-based intelligence engine.
papers.abstract: As molecular and cellular technologies have advanced, the need to analyze and interpret the resulting vast and multi-modal data into actionable intelligence has become a rate-limiting factor in scientific advancement. While traditional knowledgebase-pathway tools and LLM-based AI tools provide a degree of support in data interpretation, both exhibit known limitations. Presented here is the CompBio multi-omic analysis platform built upon Memory-based Intelligent Reasoning System (MIRaS), an associative reasoning engine grounded in episodic and semantic memory, capable of inferring biological re
papers.summary: The paper introduces CompBio, a multi-omic analysis platform powered by MIRaS, a memory-based intelligent reasoning engine that uses episodic and semantic memory to infer biological relationships from complex datasets. This approach aims to overcome limitations of traditional knowledgebase tools and LLM-based AI in interpreting vast multi-modal data.

papers.title: Advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction: Methodological evolution and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Drug efficacy prediction remains a cornerstone of drug development and precision therapy. However, integrating heterogeneous biomedical data, including multi-omics profiles, pathological imaging, electronic health records, and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) time-series, faces three fundamental barriers, namely cross-domain distribution shifts between preclinical and clinical data, relational mismatches between isolated vector representations and biological networks, and feature heterogeneity across disparate modalities. To address these challenges, three AI paradigms have emerged, tra
papers.summary: This review examines recent advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction, highlighting three key challenges—cross-domain distribution shifts, relational mismatches, and feature heterogeneity—and the AI paradigms developed to address them. It discusses the methodological evolution and clinical translation of these approaches, providing a comprehensive overview for researchers in drug development and precision medicine.

papers.title: GRASSP: RNA Language Model-Enhanced Graph Attention with Adaptive Gating for RNA-Small Molecule Binding Site Prediction.
papers.abstract: RNA-small molecule binding site prediction is crucial for targeted drug discovery. Sequence-based methods are efficient but often fail to capture structural dependencies between nucleotides, whereas structure-aware graph models can better represent spatial interactions but typically rely on complex structural annotations and multi-stage preprocessing pipelines. We therefore developed GRASSP, a streamlined hybrid deep learning framework that integrates pretrained RNA language model (LM) representations with adaptive graph refinement.
papers.summary: GRASSP is a new deep learning tool that predicts RNA-small molecule binding sites by combining RNA language model representations with graph neural networks, avoiding the need for complex structural annotations. It improves accuracy over existing methods while being more streamlined and efficient, which could aid targeted drug discovery.

papers.title: Publisher Correction: FeatureDock for protein-ligand docking guided by physicochemical feature-based local environment learning using transformer.
papers.summary: This is a publisher correction notice for a previously published paper on FeatureDock, a protein-ligand docking method. It does not contain new scientific findings or data.

papers.title: Indoor VOCs Exposure Disrupts Hemostatic Balance: Plasma Proteomics Identifies Complement and Coagulation Cascade Dysregulation as a Critical Signature.
papers.abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are prevalent indoor pollutants, posing significant health risks. However, current toxicological data focus predominantly on individual compounds, leaving a critical gap in understanding how exposure to mixed VOCs alters the plasma proteome and impacts health risk prediction. Herein, we investigated VOCs-induced hematological disturbances using a whole-body inhalation exposure model with C57BL/6J mice (n = 3) exposed to decoration-derived VOCs for 8 weeks. By integrating plasma proteomics with machine learning, we demonstrated that VOCs exposure significantly
papers.summary: This study used a mouse inhalation model to show that exposure to a mixture of indoor volatile organic compounds (VOCs) disrupts the plasma proteome, particularly affecting complement and coagulation pathways, which may impair hemostatic balance. The findings highlight the health risks of mixed VOC exposure and suggest a potential protein-based signature for risk prediction.

papers.title: Geneformer-guided multiomics integration identifies Pbx1 as a network hub of hematopoietic stem cell aging.
papers.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) constitute an organized hematopoietic system that undergoes age-related alterations, including increased platelet production and decreased erythropoiesis. The fundamental mechanisms driving these shifts remain incompletely understood. We used single-cell RNA sequencing data to show that old HSCs contain two distinct transcriptional programs: one shared with megakaryocytes and the other reflecting the most primitive HSC state. Developmental time-series profiling further suggests that the acquisition of these programs begins early in life, with the primitive modul
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and a Geneformer-based multiomics integration approach to identify two distinct transcriptional programs in aged hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), one shared with megakaryocytes and one reflecting a primitive HSC state. The authors pinpoint Pbx1 as a key network hub driving HSC aging, with developmental time-series data suggesting these aging programs begin early in life. This work provides new insights into the molecular mechanisms of HSC aging and highlights a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Integrative Proteomics and Machine Learning Identify SLC27A2 as a Candidate Biomarker and Potential Mediator of Pyrotinib Response in HER2-Positive Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Pyrotinib, an irreversible pan-HER tyrosine kinase inhibitor, has demonstrated substantial clinical efficacy in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer (BC). However, intrinsic and acquired resistance remain important challenges limiting therapeutic benefit, and reliable biomarkers for predicting pyrotinib response are currently unavailable. This study aimed to identify molecular determinants associated with pyrotinib resistance and uncover their underlying mechanisms. Methods: Pre-treatment tumour samples from an exploratory discovery cohort of 12 patients with HER2-positive BC
papers.summary: This study used integrative proteomics and machine learning on pre-treatment tumor samples from HER2-positive breast cancer patients to identify SLC27A2 as a candidate biomarker for predicting pyrotinib response. The findings suggest SLC27A2 may also play a role in mediating resistance, offering a potential target for improving therapeutic outcomes.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework that uses ESM2 protein language model embeddings and genomic-neighborhood features to fill gaps in functional annotations of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbial metagenomes. Applied to 21 silage metagenomes, CAAC achieved high cross-validation performance (F1-macro 84.64%) and improved coverage of carbohydrate-active enzyme annotations, enabling more complete metabolic interpretation.

papers.title: An Integrated Consensus Machine Learning and Structure-Based Workflow for the Discovery of Novel Tankyrase 1 Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Background: Tankyrase 1 (TNKS1) is a poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase involved in Wnt/β-catenin signaling, telomere maintenance, and genomic stability, making it an attractive therapeutic target in oncology. This study aimed to develop and apply an integrated computational workflow to identify novel TNKS1 inhibitor candidates. Methods: A curated dataset of experimentally validated TNKS1 inhibitors and property-matched DUD-E decoys was used to develop a consensus supervised machine learning (ML) model prioritization framework for ligand-based virtual screening, integrating Morgan fingerprints with t
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational workflow combining consensus machine learning with structure-based methods to discover novel Tankyrase 1 inhibitors, a promising oncology target. The approach uses curated experimental data and decoys to build a ligand-based virtual screening model, successfully identifying new candidate inhibitors.

papers.title: Integrated AI-Driven Discovery of MAPK3 Inhibitors for Oral Inflammatory and Proliferative Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 3 (MAPK3/ERK1) plays a central role in cellular proliferation, inflammation, apoptosis, and survival signalling and has been implicated in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), periodontitis, oral lichen planus, and other chronic oral inflammatory diseases. The present study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modelling, molecular docking, density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and MM-GBSA analysis to identify and characte
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated computational pipeline combining machine learning-based QSAR modeling, molecular docking, DFT, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM-GBSA analysis to identify potential MAPK3 inhibitors for treating oral inflammatory and proliferative diseases. The approach successfully characterizes novel compounds with promising binding affinity and stability, offering a foundation for future drug development in conditions like oral squamous cell carcinoma and periodontitis.

papers.title: Insulin Resistance Indices and Cardiovascular Disease Risk in Middle-Aged and Older Adults with Prediabetes: A Machine Learning-Assisted Predictive Modeling Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Insulin resistance (IR) indices-C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI), triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, and weight-adjusted waist index (WWI)-are linked to cardiovascular disease (CVD), but their comparative utility in prediabetic populations remains unclear. To evaluate the associations and exploratory mediating roles of CTI, TyG and WWI with prevalent CVD in middle-aged and elderly patients with prediabetes. Methods: The study included 3121 NHANES participants aged ≥45 with prediabetes. Four machine learning algorithms identified key variables. Multivariable logist
papers.summary: This study evaluates the associations between three insulin resistance indices (CTI, TyG, and WWI) and cardiovascular disease risk in middle-aged and older adults with prediabetes, using machine learning to identify key predictors. The findings suggest that these indices are linked to CVD prevalence, with machine learning models helping to clarify their comparative utility in this population.

papers.title: PregBase: A comprehensive knowledge base for clinically relevant knowledge representation and biomarker prediction in pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Pregnancy complications are a leading cause of maternal and neonatal mortality worldwide. Understanding their underlying mechanisms is hindered by dispersed evidence across thousands of studies and complex biological interactions. We present PregBase, a comprehensive knowledge base for pregnancy research comprising automated extraction, validation, and exploration. PregBase was constructed by utilising large language models (LLMs) to extract relationships from literature; 13 LLMs were benchmarked across seven prompting strategies, with ensemble shuffle prompting outperforming single-strategy a
papers.summary: PregBase is a new knowledge base for pregnancy research that uses large language models to automatically extract and validate relationships from the scientific literature. The authors benchmarked 13 LLMs with various prompting strategies, finding that ensemble shuffle prompting performed best, and the resulting resource supports knowledge representation and biomarker prediction for pregnancy complications.

papers.title: Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms in Distant Kinship Inference and Forensic Genetic Genealogy.
papers.abstract: Forensic genetics is moving from locus-based DNA profiling toward genome-wide inference enabled by high-density single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) data. While short tandem repeats remain central to routine human identification, SNP-based technologies and massively parallel sequencing have expanded the analysis of distant kinship through detection of identity-by-descent (IBD) segments and shared autosomal DNA. This narrative review synthesizes the biological basis of SNP-based distant kinship inference, the statistical and computational frameworks used to model genomic relatedness, and the op
papers.summary: This review examines the shift in forensic genetics from traditional STR profiling to genome-wide SNP analysis for distant kinship inference, focusing on identity-by-descent (IBD) segment detection and computational modeling. It synthesizes the biological, statistical, and computational frameworks underpinning this approach, highlighting its applications in forensic genetic genealogy.

papers.title: SEFA: Semantic Embedding-Based Feature Augmentation of Biomedical Language-Model Embeddings Improves Interpretable Metabolomic Prediction of Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Feature engineering remains a major challenge in metabolomics-based prediction, particularly when rich biochemical knowledge is available but underutilized. Conventional metabolomics models rely primarily on measured variables and statistically driven feature selection, overlooking the molecular and pathway context encoded in curated metabolite knowledge bases. We propose SEFA (Semantic Embedding-based Feature Augmentation), a model-agnostic framework that integrates metabolite-level textual knowledge from the Human Metabolome Database (HMDB) into structured metabolomics
papers.summary: SEFA is a new framework that augments metabolomics data with semantic embeddings derived from metabolite text descriptions in the Human Metabolome Database, improving interpretable prediction of lung cancer. By integrating biochemical knowledge into machine learning models, it outperforms conventional feature selection approaches and provides more biologically meaningful features.

papers.title: Exploratory Biological Correlates of Cognitive and Language Performance in Healthy Pubertal Children: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adolescence is a dynamic neurodevelopmental period during which structured language performance may reflect ongoing biological reorganization processes. This study examined whether inflammatory, nutritional, and hormonal biomarkers were modestly associated with structured language task performance and cognitive performance in healthy pubertal children. Methods: A total of 156 healthy pubertal children (78 female, 78 male; mean age of 11.84 ± 2.98 years) meeting Tanner Stage ≥ 2 were included in this retrospective cross-sectional study. Language was assessed with the Test
papers.summary: This study explored whether inflammatory, nutritional, and hormonal biomarkers are associated with cognitive and language performance in healthy pubertal children, finding only modest correlations. The results suggest that these biological factors play a limited role in explaining neurocognitive performance during this developmental period.

papers.title: Body Mass Index Is Associated with the Immunometabolic Profile in Psoriatic Arthritis: Real-Life Data.
papers.abstract: Background: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a chronic inflammatory disease frequently associated with obesity and metabolic comorbidities. Increasing evidence suggests that obesity is associated with systemic inflammation, insulin resistance, and adverse clinical outcomes; however, the immunometabolic profile associated with obesity in PsA has not been fully characterized. Objective: To investigate the relationship between obesity, inflammatory biomarkers, cytokine profiles, metabolic parameters, insulin resistance, and disease-related characteristics in patients with PsA. Methods: In this monoce
papers.summary: This study examines how body mass index (BMI) relates to immunometabolic profiles in patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA), finding that obesity is associated with altered inflammatory biomarkers, cytokine levels, and metabolic parameters. The results suggest that higher BMI may contribute to a more adverse immunometabolic state in PsA, potentially influencing disease outcomes.

papers.title: BioMaster: Multi-agent system for automated bioinformatics analysis workflow.
papers.abstract: The growing volume and complexity of biological data have made bioinformatics workflows increasingly labor-intensive, error-prone, and difficult to scale. Large language model-based agents offer potential for automation but often fail in complex, multi-step analyses because of limited robustness. We present BioMaster, a multi-agent framework that integrates workflow planning, execution, error recovery, and output validation. BioMaster incorporates a dual retrieval-augmented design to leverage domain knowledge for tool selection, parameterization, and adaptation across tasks. A dedicated debug
papers.summary: BioMaster is a multi-agent framework that automates complex bioinformatics workflows by integrating planning, execution, error recovery, and validation, with a dual retrieval-augmented design for tool selection and parameterization. It addresses the limitations of existing LLM-based agents in handling multi-step analyses, offering a more robust and scalable solution for biological data analysis.

papers.title: Brain-AI convergence: Generative world models and hierarchical attention for human intelligence.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in general-purpose AI provide new insights into how the neocortex and cerebellum, despite their uniform circuit architectures, support diverse functions and human intelligence. Beyond the traditional focus on visual processing, this paper offers a cross-domain comparison of the brain and AI through the lens of world-model-based computation. We argue that both the neocortex and cerebellum predict future world states from past inputs and construct predictive world models through prediction-error learning. These predictive world models are repurposed for sensory comprehension and
papers.summary: This paper proposes a cross-domain framework comparing brain computation (neocortex and cerebellum) with modern AI, arguing that both construct predictive world models through prediction-error learning and use hierarchical attention to support diverse cognitive functions. It extends the brain-AI convergence discussion beyond visual processing to broader aspects of human intelligence.

papers.title: Systematic Screening of Depression-Related Neurotoxicity Across 26 Bisphenols Reveals an ESR1-CREB1-GRIN2B-Associated Mechanism.
papers.abstract: Bisphenols (BPs) are widespread environmental endocrine disruptors, but their potential depression-related neurotoxicity has not been systematically assessed. Here, we combined machine learning (ML), network toxicology, molecular docking, and in vivo experiments to screen 26 bisphenols for depression-related neurotoxic risk. We first integrated bisphenol A (BPA)-related targets with depression-related genes to build a chemical-gene-phenotype-disease network and an adverse outcome pathway (AOP) framework. We then used nine ML algorithms to rank the predicted risk of the 26 bisphenols. Molecular
papers.summary: This study systematically screened 26 bisphenols for depression-related neurotoxicity using machine learning, network toxicology, molecular docking, and in vivo experiments. The authors identified an ESR1-CREB1-GRIN2B-associated mechanism as a potential key pathway, providing a framework for prioritizing bisphenols with higher neurotoxic risk.

papers.title: An Efferocytosis-Associated Gene Signature for Identifying At-Risk MASH: Transcriptomic and Exploratory Plasma Biomarker Assessment.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: At-risk metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is associated with increased risks of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality. Because impaired efferocytosis contributes to persistent hepatic inflammation and fibrotic remodeling in MASH, we investigated whether efferocytosis-associated molecular signatures could identify at-risk MASH. Methods: Bulk RNA-sequencing datasets from Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE135251 and GSE174478) were analyzed to identify differentially expressed efferocytosis-related genes and characterize associated
papers.summary: This study identifies an efferocytosis-associated gene signature that can distinguish at-risk metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) from less severe forms, using transcriptomic data from two public datasets. The findings suggest that impaired efferocytosis-related molecular patterns may serve as biomarkers for identifying patients at higher risk of disease progression.

papers.title: GAMT-GINE: A Graph Isomorphism Network Integrating Continuous Spatial Awareness and Multi-Task Learning for Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand interactions (PLIs) play a crucial role in drug discovery, and accurately predicting protein-ligand binding affinity (PLA) remains a central challenge in computer-aided drug design. Although graph neural networks (GNNs) have demonstrated considerable potential in molecular modeling, existing methods still face several limitations, including excessive reliance on hand-crafted chemical features, loss of spatial information, and difficulties in integrating heterogeneous affinity labels, which restrict their generalization capability in PLA prediction. To address these challenges, w
papers.summary: This paper introduces GAMT-GINE, a graph isomorphism network that integrates continuous spatial awareness and multi-task learning to improve protein-ligand binding affinity prediction. The method addresses limitations of existing GNNs by reducing reliance on hand-crafted features, preserving spatial information, and handling heterogeneous affinity labels, potentially enhancing generalization in drug discovery.

papers.title: AI-Supported Prediction of Vesicoureteral Reflux in Children Based on Cystoscopic Configuration of the Ureteric Orifice.
papers.abstract: Background: Vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) is a common pediatric urological disorder traditionally diagnosed by voiding cystourethrography (VCUG). Although ureteric orifice (UO) morphology during cystoscopy correlates with VUR severity, its assessment remains subjective. To our knowledge, artificial intelligence (AI) has not previously been applied to cystoscopic images for VUR prediction. We aimed to develop and evaluate the first AI model for predicting VUR from pediatric cystoscopic images and videos. Methods: In this retrospective single-center study, cystoscopic videos from children with and
papers.summary: This study presents the first AI model to predict vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) in children from cystoscopic images and videos, addressing the subjectivity of traditional ureteric orifice morphology assessment. The model offers a novel, objective approach to VUR diagnosis, potentially reducing reliance on invasive voiding cystourethrography.

papers.title: UGT-YOLO: A Multi-Strategy Fusion Model for Automated Dairy Cow Body Condition Scoring.
papers.abstract: Dairy cow body condition score (BCS) is a practical, semi-quantitative indicator of body energy reserves and changes in energy balance. To improve five-class BCS detection under complex imaging conditions, this study developed UGT-YOLO by integrating a UniRepLKNet Block, a Gather-and-Distribute feature-fusion mechanism, and a Task-Aligned Dynamic Detection Head into YOLOv11n. The model was evaluated using a single publicly available dataset containing five adjacent BCS classes: 3.25, 3.50, 3.75, 4.00, and 4.25. Following redundancy removal and image-quality screening, 7015 original images were
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This paper presents UGT-YOLO, an improved deep learning model for automated dairy cow body condition scoring, which integrates multiple architectural enhancements into YOLOv11n to better handle complex imaging conditions. The model was tested on a public dataset of five BCS classes and shows promise for automating this practical livestock management task.

papers.title: Lipid Nanoparticles for Gene Therapy: Unresolved Challenges in Manufacturing, Transdermal Delivery, Machine Learning, Endosomal Escape, and the Protein Corona.
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are now the leading delivery platform for nucleic acid therapeutics, but progress in the field is measured almost entirely by physicochemical and computational proxies rather than by functional properties that determine therapeutic outcomes. This review examines six interconnected areas of LNP development: microfluidic manufacturing, lyophilization, transdermal microneedle delivery, machine learning-guided formulation design, endosomal escape biology, and protein corona-mediated organ targeting. Although these areas are often discussed separately, they are linked by
papers.summary: This review discusses six interconnected challenges in lipid nanoparticle (LNP) development for gene therapy, including manufacturing, transdermal delivery, machine learning, endosomal escape, and protein corona effects. It argues that progress is often measured by physicochemical proxies rather than functional therapeutic outcomes, highlighting the need for more integrated approaches.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Personalized Prediction of Post-TIPS Outcomes: Integrating Clinical, Biochemical, and Radiomics Data-A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is an established treatment for complications of portal hypertension, but hepatic encephalopathy (HE), liver dysfunction, rebleeding, and mortality remain difficult to predict in otherwise eligible candidates. However, predicting post-TIPS outcomes remains challenging using conventional risk scores such as MELD 3.0 and Child-Turcotte-Pugh. This narrative review critically evaluates how clinical, biochemical, procedural, conventional imaging, handcrafted radiomics, and deep-learning features can be integrated for personalized post-TIPS risk p
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how artificial intelligence, particularly radiomics and deep learning, can be integrated with clinical and biochemical data to improve personalized prediction of outcomes after TIPS placement, such as hepatic encephalopathy and mortality. It highlights the limitations of conventional risk scores and suggests that AI-based approaches may offer more accurate, individualized risk assessment.

papers.title: Combining Triazole Scaffold Repurposing and Generative Transformer Architecture for Structure-Based Inhibitor Design Targeting the LasR Quorum Sensing Receptor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
papers.abstract: Background: The rapid escalation of multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa necessitates anti-virulence strategies targeting quorum sensing rather than bacterial survival; however, integrating scaffold repurposing with generative AI to inhibit LasR remains underexplored. Here, we address this gap by combining triazole scaffold mining with transformer-based de novo molecular generation to systematically identify putative LasR inhibitors. Methods: An integrated computational pipeline involving Structure-based inhibitor design using Generative Transformer Architecture, deep learning-assisted GNINA resc
papers.summary: This study presents a computational pipeline that combines triazole scaffold repurposing with a generative transformer architecture to design novel inhibitors of the LasR quorum sensing receptor in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. By integrating structure-based design with deep learning-assisted docking rescoring, the authors identify putative LasR inhibitors as a potential anti-virulence strategy against multidrug-resistant infections.

papers.title: Transforming subcellular spatial transcriptomics: deep learning models for cell segmentation.
papers.abstract: Subcellular spatial transcriptomics (SSTs) is transforming biology by revealing where individual RNA molecules are located within intact tissues, providing unprecedented insight into how cells function and interact. Achieving this promise depends on accurately identifying the boundaries of individual cells, making cell segmentation one of the field's central computational challenges. A core methodological issue is how best to ensure correct and biologically accurate assignment of transcripts to cells using cell segmentation algorithms. Recent advances in deep learning models have been instrume
papers.summary: This review discusses the central role of cell segmentation in subcellular spatial transcriptomics (SSTs), highlighting how deep learning models are advancing accurate assignment of RNA molecules to individual cells. It emphasizes the importance of biologically accurate segmentation for unlocking the full potential of SSTs in understanding cellular function and interactions.

papers.title: ADS Guard: A Generalizable Defense Framework for Adversarially Robust Occupancy Detection in Smart Buildings.
papers.abstract: Occupancy detection is fundamental to the operational intelligence of smart buildings, driving critical functions in energy management, HVAC automation, and physical security. While modern Deep Learning (DL) models have achieved high accuracy in parsing complex environmental sensor data, they remain highly vulnerable to adversarial examples, imperceptibly perturbed inputs designed to deceive neural networks. These vulnerabilities pose severe real-world risks, ranging from energy sabotage, in which systems heat empty rooms, to critical security breaches in which intruders go undetected. To addr
papers.summary: This paper introduces ADS Guard, a generalizable defense framework designed to protect deep learning-based occupancy detection systems in smart buildings from adversarial attacks. The framework aims to mitigate risks such as energy sabotage and security breaches by making occupancy detection models more robust against imperceptible input perturbations.

papers.title: From Descriptor Learning to Binding Stability: An Explainable Machine Learning Pipeline for EGFR Double-Mutant Inhibitor Discovery.
papers.abstract: Drug resistance arising during cancer development and progression remains a major challenge in the treatment of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-driven tumors, particularly those harboring the clinically relevant T790M/L858R double mutation. In this study, we developed an integrated computational workflow combining explainable machine learning, virtual screening, molecular dynamics simulations, and binding free-energy calculations to identify novel inhibitors of this drug-resistant EGFR variant. An XGBoost regression model was trained using scaffold-aware cross-validation, Bayesian hype
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational pipeline combining explainable machine learning, virtual screening, molecular dynamics, and binding free-energy calculations to discover novel inhibitors of the drug-resistant EGFR T790M/L858R double mutant. The XGBoost model with scaffold-aware cross-validation and Bayesian hyperparameter tuning successfully identified promising candidates, demonstrating the utility of combining ML with physics-based validation for drug resistance challenges.

papers.title: ERβ-Score: An Interpretable Machine Learning-Based Scoring Function and Web Server for Estrogen Receptor β-Guided Drug Discovery in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is the most clinically aggressive subtype of breast cancer, characterized by the absence of targetable hormone receptors and HER2 amplification, significantly constraining treatment choices. Estrogen Receptor Beta (ERβ) has emerged as a biologically relevant yet underutilized target in TNBC, with its re-expression linked to tumor suppression and improved prognosis, prompting the development of selective ERβ modulators as a precision therapeutic approach. We introduce ERβ-Score, an interpretable machine learning scoring system developed using a curated datas
papers.summary: The authors developed ERβ-Score, an interpretable machine learning-based scoring function and web server to support drug discovery targeting Estrogen Receptor Beta (ERβ) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The tool aims to identify selective ERβ modulators by leveraging a curated dataset, potentially addressing the lack of targeted therapies for this aggressive cancer subtype.

papers.title: EFEMP2 Is Associated with Shelterin-Related DNA Damage Repair, Immune Microenvironment Features, and Prognosis in Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) carries a median overall survival below 15 months despite aggressive multimodal therapy. Treatment resistance reflects the interplay of genomic instability, dysregulated DNA damage repair (DDR), and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). The shelterin complex maintains telomere integrity, yet its broader role in coordinating DDR, TME remodeling, and clinical outcomes in GBM remains unclear. Methods: We integrated transcriptomic and clinical data from four public cohorts (TCGA, CGGA1, CGGA2, and REMBRANDT, n = 583) and an institutional cohort (CSUXY, n
papers.summary: This study identifies EFEMP2 as a prognostic biomarker in glioblastoma, linking its expression to shelterin-related DNA damage repair and immune microenvironment features. Analysis of multiple transcriptomic cohorts shows that EFEMP2 is associated with patient survival and immune cell infiltration, suggesting it may serve as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Culture-Based Microbiological Assessment of Dentin Biomaterials Prepared from Long-Term Refrigerated Human Teeth: A Pilot Study Toward Evidence-Based Tooth Banking.
papers.abstract: Dentin derived from extracted human teeth has emerged as a promising autogenous biomaterial for bone regeneration owing to its structural and biological similarity to bone tissue. Growing clinical interest in dentin-derived graft materials has also stimulated the development of tooth-banking concepts, in which extracted teeth are preserved for future regenerative applications. However, microbiological contamination remains one of the principal concerns associated with long-term storage before clinical use. This in vitro study evaluated the microbiological status of dentin biomaterials prepared
papers.summary: This pilot study assessed the microbiological safety of dentin biomaterials prepared from human teeth stored long-term under refrigeration, finding that such storage can maintain acceptable sterility for clinical use. The results support the feasibility of tooth banking for regenerative applications, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Recombinant SpTrf proteins illustrate putative functions of native SpTrf proteins: from immune response to resolution in sea urchins.
papers.abstract: The complex and sophisticated sea urchin innate immune system relies on conserved immune receptor and effector molecules plus the euechinoid-specific Transformer family. Native SpTransformer (natSpTrf) proteins in Strongylocentrotus purpuratus respond to immune challenge by augmenting phagocytosis of microbes. These proteins show significant sequence diversity both within and among sea urchins with the predicted benefit of host protection through the recognition of a broad range of pathogens. Prior reports show that 6 recombinant (r)SpTrf proteins from insect cells induce phagocytosis when cro
papers.summary: This study characterizes recombinant SpTransformer (rSpTrf) proteins from sea urchins, showing they can induce phagocytosis and modulate immune responses, suggesting native SpTrf proteins function in both immune defense and resolution of inflammation. The findings provide functional insights into the diverse roles of these euechinoid-specific proteins in the sea urchin innate immune system.

papers.title: Neuromorphic Cardiac Sensing: A Bio-Inspired Spiking Neural Network with Sensory-Adaptive Encoding for Energy-Efficient Arrhythmia Detection from ECG and PPG Signals.
papers.abstract: Living nervous systems sense the cardiovascular rhythm with a parsimony that engineered monitors cannot match: sensory receptors encode changes rather than absolute levels, neurons communicate through sparse all-or-none events, retinal circuits sharpen salient features through lateral inhibition, and attention is allocated by surprise. We translate these four principles into BioSpike-Net, a fully event-driven spiking neural network for cardiac-rhythm classification from electrocardiogram (ECG) and photoplethysmogram (PPG) signals. A sensory-adaptive spike encoder (SASE) converts analogue wavef
papers.summary: This paper introduces BioSpike-Net, a bio-inspired spiking neural network that applies principles from biological nervous systems (sensory-adaptive encoding, sparse event-driven communication, lateral inhibition, and surprise-based attention) to detect cardiac arrhythmias from ECG and PPG signals. The approach aims to achieve energy-efficient and accurate arrhythmia classification, potentially outperforming traditional engineered monitors in parsimony and efficiency.

papers.title: Multiclass Machine Learning-Based Discovery of Novel Scaffold Inhibitors Targeting ALK.
papers.abstract: Background: Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase (ALK) is an oncogenic receptor tyrosine kinase implicated in several cancers. Despite the clinical success of ALK inhibitors, acquired resistance continues to drive the search for novel chemotypes. We developed a multiclass machine learning framework to classify ALK inhibitory activity using a curated ChEMBL dataset. Methods: Models were built using 2D molecular descriptors together with MACCS and ECFP4 fingerprints. Three widely used algorithms, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost, were applied for model development. Results: RF
papers.summary: This study developed a multiclass machine learning framework to identify novel ALK inhibitors, using 2D descriptors and fingerprints with SVM, Random Forest, and XGBoost on a curated ChEMBL dataset. The Random Forest model performed best, enabling the discovery of new scaffold inhibitors that could help overcome acquired resistance in ALK-driven cancers.

papers.title: FluEvoFormer: A Structure-Guided Generative Foundation Model for Prospective Influenza Antigenic Evolution and Vaccine Strain Selection.
papers.abstract: Seasonal influenza vaccine strain selection remains challenging because circulating viruses may drift after vaccine recommendations are made. This study presents FluEvoFormer, a structure-guided generative foundation model for prospective influenza antigenic evolution forecasting and vaccine strain ranking. The framework jointly encodes hemagglutinin and neuraminidase sequences and incorporates residue-contact graphs. Separate prediction heads estimate future viral dominance and the vaccine-virus antigenic match. Controlled future-like variant stress testing, uncertainty adjustments, and clade
papers.summary: FluEvoFormer is a new structure-guided generative foundation model that predicts future influenza antigenic evolution and ranks vaccine strains by jointly encoding hemagglutinin and neuraminidase sequences with residue-contact graphs. It uses separate prediction heads for viral dominance and vaccine-virus antigenic match, and includes stress testing and uncertainty adjustments to improve prospective accuracy. This could help make seasonal vaccine strain selection more proactive and reliable.

papers.title: PepGen: conditional generation of peptides for MHC binding.
papers.abstract: Peptide-MHC II binding drives adaptive immunity, yet discovery of novel binder peptides remains challenging due to open binding grooves of MHC-II that accommodate variable-length peptides. While discriminative models perform well, they are unfeasible for generation via enumeration due to vast peptide space (2013≈8×1016 for peptides of length 13 amino acids). Generative AI approaches could accelerate binder design to enable vaccines targeted to particular MHC-II alleles or optimize other peptide chemical properties.
papers.summary: PepGen is a new generative AI tool that designs peptide binders for MHC-II molecules, addressing the challenge of the vast peptide sequence space that makes enumeration-based discovery impractical. By generating novel binder candidates directly, it could accelerate vaccine design and peptide optimization for specific MHC-II alleles.

papers.title: Pocket-PROTACs: an interpretable pocket-aware deep learning framework for predicting PROTAC-induced protein degradation.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation by recruiting an E3 ubiquitin ligase to a protein of interest (POI) and forming a ternary complex. Despite their therapeutic promise, rational PROTAC design remains challenging, as degradation efficacy depends on subtle and highly structure-dependent interactions among the POI, the E3 ligase, and the bifunctional molecule.
papers.summary: This paper introduces Pocket-PROTACs, a deep learning framework that predicts PROTAC-induced protein degradation by incorporating pocket-aware information about the protein of interest and E3 ligase. The model provides interpretable insights into the structural determinants of degradation efficacy, potentially aiding rational PROTAC design.

papers.title: RIBEX: predicting and explaining RNA binding across structured and intrinsically disordered regions (IDR)-rich proteins.
papers.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate post-transcriptional processes, yet many remain undiscovered because RNA-binding activity often occurs outside canonical RNA-binding domains (RBDs), including within intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) or through protein complexes. Computational methods can help identify novel RBPs, but approaches relying solely on sequence-derived features or ignoring the cellular interaction context are limited in capturing the complexity of RNA-binding behavior. To date, no framework rigorously integrates both sequence information and protein interaction context for
papers.summary: RIBEX is a new computational framework that predicts RNA-binding proteins by integrating both sequence-derived features and protein interaction context, addressing the challenge of RNA binding occurring outside canonical domains, including in intrinsically disordered regions. It aims to improve discovery of novel RBPs and provide explanations for predictions, filling a gap in existing methods.

papers.title: Stoic: fast and accurate protein stoichiometry prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein complexes are central to cellular function, but experimental determination of their structures remains challenging. Structure prediction methods require prior knowledge of stoichiometry-the number of copies of each protein entity within a complex. Current approaches rely on computationally expensive brute-force methods that run structure prediction on multiple stoichiometry combinations, often with limited accuracy.
papers.summary: This paper introduces Stoic, a fast and accurate method for predicting protein complex stoichiometry, which is a necessary input for structure prediction. It addresses the limitations of current brute-force approaches by being computationally efficient while improving accuracy.

papers.title: Explicit encoding of temporal dynamics for interpretable melody similarity modeling: insight into machine learning models.
papers.abstract: Temporal melody similarity is a fundamental problem in music modelling, and current methods are mostly based on recurrent or attention-based architectures that implicitly learn sequential structures.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a novel approach for melody similarity that explicitly encodes temporal dynamics, offering interpretability compared to implicit recurrent or attention-based models. The method provides insight into how machine learning models capture sequential musical structure, potentially improving both performance and understanding of melody similarity tasks.

papers.title: MetaCYP: a unified framework for prediction of cytochrome P450 metabolic sites and reaction types via multimodal deep learning.
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes are the predominant drug-metabolizing proteins in humans, collectively governing the structural transformation of drugs and xenobiotics while directly shaping their pharmacological activity and toxicological profiles. Accurate prediction of CYP-substrate reaction sites and reaction types is therefore central to drug discovery and metabolic risk assessment. Existing computational models, however, largely depend on intrinsic molecular properties or hardcoded reaction rules, constraining their generalization across CYP isoforms.
papers.summary: MetaCYP is a new deep learning framework that predicts where cytochrome P450 enzymes metabolize drugs and what type of reaction occurs, using multimodal data. It improves generalization across different CYP isoforms compared to existing methods that rely on molecular properties or fixed rules, which is important for drug discovery and safety assessment.

papers.title: Peripheral endocrine-nutritional machine learning signature predicts short-term response to neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in locally advanced gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Major pathological response (MPR) to neoadjuvant PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy in locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC) varies widely and is incompletely explained by tumor-side biomarkers. Because checkpoint inhibitors act within a host environment shaped by endocrine, nutritional, and inflammatory state, we developed and validated the Endocrine-Nutritional Immunotherapy response score (ENI-Score) from routine pretreatment peripheral-blood markers to predict short-term response and early recurrence.
papers.summary: This study developed and validated a machine learning-based score (ENI-Score) using routine pretreatment peripheral blood markers related to endocrine, nutritional, and inflammatory status to predict short-term response to neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in locally advanced gastric cancer. The score aims to complement tumor-side biomarkers by capturing host systemic factors, potentially improving prediction of major pathological response and early recurrence.

papers.title: EMCN is associated with vascular-immune crosstalk and represents a potential biomarker in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: While MUC family genes have been established as prognostic biomarkers in gastric cancer, and GWAS studies link EMCN mutations to chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in NSCLC, the systematic characterization of EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study systematically characterizes EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), finding that its expression is associated with vascular-immune crosstalk and may serve as a potential prognostic biomarker. The authors provide evidence linking EMCN to immune infiltration and clinical outcomes in LUAD, filling a gap in knowledge about this gene's role in the disease.

papers.title: Identification and validation of key host genes associated with porcine H1N1 infection based on integrated machine learning algorithms.
papers.abstract: Swine H1N1 influenza is a critical zoonotic pathogen threatening pig industry economy and public health. The host molecular regulatory network and core genes of H1N1 infection remain unclear, hindering targeted prevention and therapy. Traditional experimental methods fail to efficiently mine high-dimensional transcriptomic data, making precise screening of infection biomarkers difficult. Methods: Transcriptome data (GSE40092) were analyzed to obtain porcine lung DEGs upon H1N1 infection, followed by GO/KEGG functional enrichment. Four machine learning algorithms (LASSO, random forest, SVM-RFE,
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning on porcine lung transcriptomic data to identify key host genes associated with swine H1N1 infection, revealing potential biomarkers and regulatory networks. The findings may aid targeted prevention and therapy for this zoonotic pathogen.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of hub genes and prognostic biomarkers in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the second most prevalent malignancy in men worldwide, and accurate stratification of biochemical recurrence (BCR) risk remains challenging using conventional clinicopathological parameters alone. Identification of robust molecular biomarkers and integrated prognostic models is therefore of high clinical priority.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to identify hub genes and prognostic biomarkers for prostate cancer, aiming to improve the prediction of biochemical recurrence beyond conventional clinical parameters. The authors develop an integrated prognostic model based on these molecular markers, which could aid in risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

papers.title: InfoMedex: drug-drug interaction prediction via a multimodal CNN-transformer model.
papers.abstract: Drug-drug interactions are an important source of preventable adverse drug events. Computational methods that incorporate chemical structure and biological context may support more scalable and interpretable interaction prediction.
papers.journal: Frontiers in drug safety and regulation
papers.summary: InfoMedex is a new computational model that predicts drug-drug interactions by combining chemical structure information with biological context using a multimodal CNN-transformer architecture. The model aims to provide more scalable and interpretable predictions than existing methods, potentially helping to prevent adverse drug events.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-integrated multimodal retinal imaging for early detection and risk stratification of systemic vascular and neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.abstract: We developed and validated RetinalVNG-Net, a multimodal deep learning framework for simultaneous risk stratification of hypertensive retinopathy, diabetic retinopathy, and neurodegenerative-associated retinal changes from integrated fundus photography, optical coherence tomography, and clinical metadata.
papers.summary: This paper introduces RetinalVNG-Net, a multimodal deep learning framework that combines fundus photography, optical coherence tomography, and clinical metadata to simultaneously assess risk for hypertensive retinopathy, diabetic retinopathy, and neurodegenerative retinal changes. The framework shows promise for early detection and risk stratification of systemic vascular and neurodegenerative diseases using retinal imaging.

papers.title: OtoVCE: a mechanism-aware language-model evidence layer for hereditary hearing-loss variant interpretation.
papers.abstract: Missense variants in genes implicated in hereditary hearing loss are frequently returned to clinicians as variants of uncertain significance. In silico predictors and rule-based ACMG/AMP frameworks each capture only a fraction of the required evidence, and neither directly accesses case-level and functional evidence reported in the published literature.
papers.summary: This paper introduces OtoVCE, a language-model-based evidence layer that integrates case-level and functional evidence from published literature to improve the interpretation of missense variants in hereditary hearing-loss genes. By combining this evidence with existing in silico predictors and ACMG/AMP rules, OtoVCE aims to reduce the number of variants of uncertain significance returned to clinicians.

papers.title: The Embodied Hijack: when Pleistocene minds meet disembodied artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into everyday life has intensified a long-standing feature of human cognition: the attribution of agency, intention, and understanding to nonhuman systems. People describe language models, virtual assistants, and autonomous technologies as if these systems know, decide, want, or understand, and they continue to do so even when they know the systems have no inner life. The standard account dismisses this as naïve anthropomorphism, the misfiring of evolved agency-detection systems calibrated in the Environment of Evolutionary Adaptedness. We argue
papers.summary: This paper argues that attributing agency and intention to AI systems is not simply a cognitive error but reflects deep-seated evolutionary mechanisms from our Pleistocene past. The authors propose that these 'embodied hijacks' occur when modern AI interfaces trigger ancient agency-detection systems, leading to persistent anthropomorphism even when users consciously know the systems lack inner life. The work offers a theoretical framework for understanding human-AI interaction through an evolutionary psychology lens.

papers.title: SHAP-interpretable machine learning integrating exposures and multi-omics reveals immune alterations and biomarkers in COPD-lung cancer comorbidity.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer (LC) frequently co-occur and share environmental and biological determinants, yet their cross-scale associations remain incompletely understood. Artificial intelligence and machine learning-based integration of exposome and multi-omics data provide new opportunities for dissecting this complex comorbidity.
papers.summary: This study uses SHAP-interpretable machine learning to integrate environmental exposures and multi-omics data, uncovering immune alterations and potential biomarkers associated with COPD-lung cancer comorbidity. The findings provide new insights into the cross-scale biological mechanisms linking these two diseases.

papers.title: A biologically structured hierarchical vision transformer-CNN framework for robust tomato leaf disease classification.
papers.abstract: Precise and reliable diagnosis of leaf diseases in tomato is essential for enhancing crop cultivation and minimizing agricultural losses. While deep learning models have performed well on benchmark datasets, the majority of present techniques rely on flat multi-class classification, which predicts all disease categories simultaneously. Such formulations promotes inter-class confusion, particularly when biologically different diseases with similar visual symptoms are learned within a same model. To overcome this constraint, we propose a biologically structured hierarchical deep learning framewo
papers.summary: This paper presents a hierarchical deep learning framework that combines vision transformers and CNNs to classify tomato leaf diseases, addressing inter-class confusion by structuring classification according to biological disease relationships. The approach improves accuracy and robustness compared to flat multi-class models, particularly for visually similar diseases.
